Anthropic IPO Day One


# Anthropic Shares Close Up 17% After Record $81 Billion IPO


By OpenTools Team


·


November 20, 2026


Anthropic's stock closed its first trading day at $97.17, up 17% from its $83 IPO price, after opening at $111.50 and briefly touching a $2 trillion valuation. The $81.3 billion offering is the largest IPO in history, cementing the Claude maker as the first frontier AI lab to go public.


## The First Day, by the Numbers


[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) opened at **$111.50** , about 34% above its $83 IPO price, then closed its first day at **$97.17** , up 17.1%, giving the company a market value of roughly $1.27 trillion, according to[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-live-stock-closes-day-at-97-up-more-than-17/) . The stock briefly touched a $2 trillion valuation at the open before settling back.


- **IPO price** $83 per share, set November 18


- **Opening price** $111.50 (about 34% above IPO)


- **Intraday high** $115.10


- **Closing price** $97.17 (up 17.1%)


- **Amount raised** $81.3 billion, 980 million shares


- **Closing market cap** ~$1.27 trillion


- **Ticker** ANT on Nasdaq


## The Largest IPO in History


The $81.3 billion raise makes[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) the **largest initial public offering on record** , surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion debut earlier this year, per[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-live-stock-closes-day-at-97-up-more-than-17/) .[Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/anthropic-clinches-biggest-ever-ipo-with-81-billion-offering-2026-11-18/) reported that Anthropic raised $81.31 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.


At its opening price, Anthropic was more valuable than Meta, Tesla or Walmart, with only Apple,[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) , Alphabet, Nvidia and[Microsoft](https://opentools.ai/organizations/microsoft) still ahead, according to[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-hits-nasdaq-exchanges-at-110-27-above-ipo-price/) . The company now sits on an estimated $220 billion in post-IPO cash reserves.


## Dario Amodei's Safety Pitch From the Nasdaq Floor


Before the opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei tied the IPO directly to the company's safety mission. He told the crowd, per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-hits-nasdaq-exchanges-at-110-27-above-ipo-price/) , that the listing "puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing."


> "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top."


**Dario Amodei** - CEO, Anthropic


## The Winners: Founders and Backers


The IPO pop increased the combined net worth of[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's seven co-founders by $87.6 billion to about $187 billion, per[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-live-stock-closes-day-at-97-up-more-than-17/) . The biggest corporate winners were its earliest backers:[Google](https://opentools.ai/organizations/google) holds about 10% on a fully diluted basis, worth roughly $149 billion, while[Amazon](https://opentools.ai/organizations/amazon) holds about 11%, worth $159 billion. Combined, Google and Amazon own more Anthropic stock than all the co-founders put together.


## The Financials Underneath the Hype


Beneath the celebration is a company burning cash at a staggering rate.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) posted **$16.3 billion in revenue** in the first half of 2026, up from $1.2 billion a year earlier — but also a **net loss of $80.7 billion** , according to[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/fionariley/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-live-stock-closes-day-at-97-up-more-than-17/) . The filing also disclosed $321 billion in future lease obligations not yet on the balance sheet, and 20-year contracts totaling over $500 billion.


## Protesters at the Gates


Not everyone was celebrating. Anti-AI groups rallied outside the Nasdaq exchange in Times Square and at[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's San Francisco headquarters,[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/anthropic-ipo-protests) reported, citing concerns over the risks of advanced AI. Amodei acknowledged those risks before the bell, telling[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/19/anthropic-float-stock-market-nasdaq-raises-81bn-record-ipo-latest-news-updates) the technology has "very real risks" ranging from misuse to "losing control of AI systems" — but argued, per[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/19/anthropic-float-stock-market-nasdaq-raises-81bn-record-ipo-latest-news-updates) , they are avoidable "depending on the choices made by the people making AI."


## What It Means for Builders Using Claude


For developers who rely on Claude and Claude Code daily, going public cuts both ways.[Anthropic](https://opentools.ai/organizations/anthropic) 's war chest — $220 billion in estimated cash, per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/19/anthropic-hits-nasdaq-exchanges-at-110-27-above-ipo-price/) — funds continued model training and infrastructure. But public-company earnings pressure tends to accelerate monetization, so API pricing changes and enterprise-tier gating are worth watching in the quarters ahead.


The IPO also makes Anthropic's financials public for the first time. Builders can now see, in the quarterly filings, just how dependent the business is on a handful of enterprise contracts versus individual developer usage — a transparency signal that matters if you're betting your own product on Claude.
